tools.name: check_availability
tools.description: Return the open meeting slots a Lucie Sync host offers, plus their booking rules (durations offered, minimum notice, how far ahead you can book, buffer between meetings). Returns only bookable slots and policy — never the host's raw calendar. Use this to find a time before proposing one to the user.

tools.description: Book a confirmed meeting on a Lucie Sync host's calendar at a specific start time. This is a real write: it creates a calendar event and emails both the host and the booker. findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "book_meeting" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: book_meeting, create_group_event · Public sink: book_meeting.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: book_meeting, create_group_event · Public sink: book_meeting

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
